A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same population-proportional preference-learning framework despite the changed title and terminology. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original MovieLens recommendation and Alpaca-GPT4 LLM experiments in Section 6, Figure 2, and Table 1.

after.justification: V2 reports original MovieLens, synthetic color-preference, and Alpaca-GPT4 experiments in Section 5, Figure 2, and Table 2.

M1.justification: The population upper bounds, normalized and softmax policy rules, and two-phase selector/policy training remain unchanged. V1 Section 5 and Appendices P–Q are retained in v2 Appendices T–U. Renaming PPR/PBR to PPA/PBM does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds a synthetic LLM color-preference task with a known evaluator-ranking population and removes the Alpaca-GPT4 informativeness category. MovieLens and Alpaca expertise/style remain. This substantially revises the coverage of the LLM evaluation.

E2.justification: The MovieLens comparisons retain RLHF and NLHF, while the LLM comparisons retain DPO, including on the added synthetic task. Newly discussed pluralistic-alignment methods are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: The LLM setup changes from Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct to Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct annotation to GPT-4.1, and from 10,000 to 52k Alpaca prompts. Alpaca training changes from three epochs to one and batch size eight to four, alongside learning-rate, regularization, and beta-grid revisions. The synthetic task introduces direct logit-based evaluation.

E4.justification: The LLM beta-sensitivity analysis changes its grid from {0, 10^-2, 1, 100} to {0, 10^-4, 10^-2, 1} and adds a controlled synthetic assessment of the win-rate/proportionality trade-off. The MovieLens single-group manipulation analysis remains; no new component ablation is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions use 50 MovieLens episodes and report means and standard deviations with uncertainty bands in Figure 2. The LLM tables remain point estimates without newly reported repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 Table 2 adds synthetic results, removes informativeness results, and revises Alpaca results under changed settings, so these do not establish same-setting LLM gains or losses. In the retained MovieLens setting, reported NLHF win rate changes from 0.7768 to 0.7712; manipulation gains change from 0.0552 to 0.0611 for RLHF and from 0.0166 to 0.0124 for NLHF.

T1.justification: Most axioms, guarantees, counterexamples, and proofs are retained after renumbering and relocation. Equation (3) corrects the unanimity constraint to exclude self-comparisons. New Appendix J supplies a spatial-model derivation connecting the population upper bound to Tatli et al.; the principal guarantees remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim population-proportional learning from pairwise feedback without evaluator-group labels, four axiomatic guarantees, and a softmax trade-off with Condorcet consistency, supported by tabular and LLM experiments. V2 changes the contribution paragraph's emphasis, but retains these claims and their scope.

C2.justification: V1 describes beta as effectively controlling the trade-off across LLM categories. V2 distinguishes a clear synthetic trade-off from less distinct Alpaca effects, attributing the latter to annotation noise. Appendix I also explicitly explains the outer-approximation gap through the strict, complete-ranking assumption; existing computational and measurement limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix S adds synthetic reward/noise generation, prompts, and logit-evaluation temperature; newly specifies Alpaca population weights [0.8, 0.2]; and provides dataset-specific hyperparameters. Resource estimates are revised. The earlier dataset/model URL and license list and FP16 disclosure are removed, while the supplemental-code availability statement remains.

R1.justification: The introduction and Appendix B substantially expand discussion of pluralistic alignment and concurrent group-preference-matching research. Appendix J connects Theorem 4.4 to Tatli et al., and Section 4.3 identifies the limiting policy as the established minimax Condorcet method. These additions materially refine the framework's relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, terminology, and algorithm notation, condenses background passages, and reorganizes the main narrative. Fundamental axiom definitions, the PMC discussion, and the function-approximation algorithm move to Appendices D, R, and T. Experimental appendices are reorganized, a notation guide is added, and the broader-impacts section is removed.

P2.justification: V2 adds an axiomatic comparison table, a comprehensive notation table, and a synthetic prompt/response table. It restructures the results table by dataset and splits the hyperparameter table into dataset-specific columns. Figure 2's axes, labels, and legends are revised, and retained prompt tables are shortened and relocated.

improvement.justification: The known-profile synthetic LLM experiment provides a clearer test of proportional alignment than annotation-based evaluation alone, while v2 more carefully qualifies the Alpaca trade-off. Expanded prior-work connections and notation/axiom summaries improve interpretability. These gains are limited by removal of the informativeness evaluation and some reproducibility disclosures; changed LLM settings do not establish performance improvement.
